title: Sharjah City Guide: 18 Contemporary and Historical Attractions to Discover in UAE's Cultural Hub
text:
Sharjah City Guide: 18 Contemporary and Historical Attractions to Discover in UAE's Cultural Hub

Sharjah, the captivating territory in the United Arab Emirates, is a cultural hub that blends tradition with contemporary modernity. Situated on the Arabian coastline, the city is known for its commitment to preserving its rich history, promoting the arts and culture, and providing a platform for creative and intellectual pursuits. In fact, the 2023 Sharjah Architecture Triennial (SAT) will take place from November 11, 2023, to March 10, 2024, under the theme "The Beauty of Impermanence: An Architecture of Adaptability." The Triennial is curated by Tosin Oshinowo, exploring innovative design solutions emerging from conditions of scarcity in the Global South.

title: What to Consider When Integrating Photovoltaics into Building Facades
text:
What to Consider When Integrating Photovoltaics into Building Facades

When considering building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV), the potential is clear: making the building envelope an active part of a building's energy strategy. Yet specifying these systems can be difficult when the process is unfamiliar. How much electricity can a facade generate? What will the system cost? Which orientations and areas are suitable? And how should the photovoltaic panels be integrated with the building's structural, electrical, and fire-safety requirements? Without clear answers, assessing feasibility, establishing budgets, and involving consultants and contractors can become difficult.

title: Sydney’s Powerhouse Parramatta Museum and Bratislava’s Winter Harbour Redevelopment: This Week’s Review
text:
Sydney’s Powerhouse Parramatta Museum and Bratislava’s Winter Harbour Redevelopment: This Week’s Review

This week's stories focus on cultural architecture and the ways museums, art institutions, and public venues are being designed, expanded, and adapted. Across different cities, new projects bring together exhibition spaces, educational programmes, and areas for public activity, while existing buildings take on new cultural uses. From Sydney and Sharjah to Miami and Dubai, the projects reflect a range of approaches to creating and extending spaces for art and culture, with attention to their programmes, audiences, and connections to the surrounding urban environment.

title: Les Balcons de Sermenaz / HEMAA Architectes
text:
Les Balcons de Sermenaz / HEMAA Architectes

Located along the ridge between the Rhône and Saône rivers, Rillieux-la-Pape occupies a unique position within the metropolitan area. The town combines an historic village centre with numerous large residential developments that open out to the east onto an extensive protected natural area stretching along the hillside. It is at the edge of this landscape that the Les Balcons de Sermenaz residential development takes shape. As the final component of a new neighborhood, it forms a link with the park and accompanies the gradual transition from the urban fabric to the natural environment. This unusual setting oﬀers the opportunity to build in direct relationship with a largely preserved landscape.

title: A Glass Labyrinth by Ciro Najle and Josep Ferrando Opens at the Barcelona Pavilion
text:
A Glass Labyrinth by Ciro Najle and Josep Ferrando Opens at the Barcelona Pavilion

An artistic intervention opens today, November 12, 2026, at the Barcelona Pavilion. A modernist icon, the building was designed by Mies van der Rohe and Lilly Reich for the 1929 International Exposition in Barcelona, Spain, to represent modern Germany after World War I. The building was originally designed to be temporary and is now managed by the Fundació Mies van der Rohe, created in 1983 by the Barcelona City Council to reconstruct it. Since its rebuilding, the pavilion has been open to visitors as an architectural landmark and is occasionally used as a venue for interventions by visual artists and short-term exhibitions. From November 12 to 22, 2026, "Pavilion-Labyrinth" by Ciro Najle and Josep Ferrando will lead visitors into a labyrinth made entirely of glass, transforming the perceived boundaries between the interior and exterior of the historic building.

title: Which Materials Meet the Demands of a Contemporary Kitchen?
text:
Which Materials Meet the Demands of a Contemporary Kitchen?

The contemporary kitchen is no longer just a space for food preparation; it has become one of the most dynamic areas of the home. Design decisions can redefine both spatial configurations and the arrangement of individual elements as kitchens become integrated with social areas, incorporate new technologies, and adapt to changing domestic habits. In this way, balancing functionality, comfort, durability, and aesthetics is closely tied to the selection of finishing materials. From countertop surfaces to cabinet opening systems, each design choice contributes to creating kitchen environments that accommodate different activities and ways of living.

title: Before the Urban Grid: The Colonial City of Santo Domingo in Dominican Republic
text:
Before the Urban Grid: The Colonial City of Santo Domingo in Dominican Republic

The Dominican Republic occupies the eastern portion of Hispaniola, an island in the Greater Antilles of the Caribbean that it shares with neighbouring Haiti. On the Dominican Republic's southern coast, at the mouth of the Ozama River, stands Santo Domingo, the country's capital and the first permanent European settlement in the Americas. This distinction has earned Santo Domingo the title of "Ciudad Primada", or First City, as well as a UNESCO World Heritage listing, for being one of the earliest records of how Europeans first approached the organization of urban settlements in the New World.

Hotel I & II, Tsuyama is a pair of small hotels created through the renovation of two machiya townhouses in the Joto area of Tsuyama, Okayama Prefecture, Japan. The district is a historic townscape where traditional townhouses line the former Izumo Kaido road. Within this setting, the project converts two wooden houses into small hotels: Hotel I with a lobby and gallery, and Hotel II with a cafe, each with two guest rooms above.

text:
Casa Fogo / Pablo Patriota Arquitetos Associados

The most challenging lots are my best friends. In my view of the design craft, challenges naturally lead to solutions. The difficult topography of the terrain in Serra Negra, in Bezerros, Pernambuco, the giant boulder embedded in it, the trees that had to be preserved, the clearing where I could place the construction, and the best views all guided how the project should take shape.

title: Freedom Mobile Arch Amphitheatre / Revery Architecture
text:
Freedom Mobile Arch Amphitheatre / Revery Architecture

Framing views of Vancouver's North Shore Mountains, the Freedom Mobile Arch is an open-air amphitheatre designed to remain connected to its surrounding landscape. A sweeping mass-timber canopy shelters audiences of up to 10,000 while preserving the experience of being outdoors. Permanent infrastructure and adaptable seating allow the venue to accommodate performances and gatherings at a wide range of scales.

title: Danubio Budapest Building / T2.a Architects
text:
Danubio Budapest Building / T2.a Architects

Designed by T2a Architects and completed recently on the site of a former river gravel pit on the banks of the Danube in Budapest, the Danubio residential building responds to the unique urban and natural environment, partially overriding the rules of Budapest real estate developers, and realizes a concept that treats sustainability not only as a slogan but also revives many pre-existing but now forgotten architectural solutions and recreates them in a modern, timeless form.

title: Planá Kindergarten  / PROAM ARCHITEKTI
text:
Planá Kindergarten / PROAM ARCHITEKTI

The new municipal kindergarten in Planá, South Bohemia, represents a sensitive yet confident introduction of modern architecture into a historic rural setting. A sustainable public building made of timber has been created on a small but visually prominent site. Its form immediately reveals its purpose—a building for children that is part traditional, part modern, and somewhat fairytale-like.

title: Building from Place: Inside the Work of RAMA Estudio
text:
Building from Place: Inside the Work of RAMA Estudio

Carla Chávez, Carolina Rodas, and Felipe Donoso began collaborating while studying architecture in Quito, Ecuador, and went on to found RAMA Estudio, one of the winners of the ArchDaily Next Practices Awards 2026. For more than a decade, their practice has moved between housing, public spaces, adaptive reuse, and community initiatives. Their work is guided by an understanding of architecture as a service. For them, a project begins with the circumstances of a place and extends to the people who will build it and those who will live with it for years.

title: Gamaya Farms / Biome Environmental Solutions
text:
Gamaya Farms / Biome Environmental Solutions

Gamaya Farms redefines architectural iconism not through bold geometry, but through absolute camouflage and tectonic erasure. Situated near Vikarabad, along a forested plateau and rolling hills, the project serves as a shared amenities zone and eco-resort for a farm-plot community. Rather than treating the program as a monolithic footprint, the master plan deconstructs the traditional resort layout into distinct, site-specific architectural typologies.

title: Sumayya Vally Unveils First Permanent UAE Project With Dubai’s Elie Khouri Art Foundation
text:
Sumayya Vally Unveils First Permanent UAE Project With Dubai’s Elie Khouri Art Foundation

The Elie Khouri Art Foundation (EKAF) has appointed Sumayya Vally of Johannesburg- and London-based practice Counterspace to design its permanent home in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Scheduled to open in late 2028, the institution will occupy a repurposed villa in the Jumeirah 1 district, transforming the existing residential property and its surrounding grounds into a space for contemporary art exhibitions, education, and public programming. The appointment forms part of EKAF's plans to establish a permanent platform for contemporary art in Dubai, with architecture and curatorial programming developed in parallel.

title: Cultural and Community Center Stara Fužina / OFIS Architects
text:
Cultural and Community Center Stara Fužina / OFIS Architects

A HOUSE BUILT BY ITS COMMUNITY Villagers and the wider local community built the cultural center in Stara Fužina in 1983 through contributions of income, materials, knowledge, and labor. The need for a shared cultural space dates back to the years after the Second World War, when the village created a temporary hall and stage in the former Zois manor. The new cultural center later provided a permanent setting for events, gatherings, and public life. Its significance therefore comes not only from the building itself, but also from the way the community created and used it over several decades. The renovation continues this principle. The existing house remains the framework for collective activity while adapting to contemporary forms of work, gathering, and cultural production.
